subject: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Cho <dana@velox.ai>, Samuel Price <sam.price@velox.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up + next steps (deployment mode qualification)

Hi Dana / Sam — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we agreed we'd follow up on: 

1) Primary deployment constraint: you said data residency and auditability are top priorities for production (no PII leaving your VPC). That pushed private VPC / on-prem as the likely long-term option, but you also asked about a hybrid path (start on Hosted API for MLP and move to Dedicated/Private as volume matures).

2) Traffic profile: rough estimate from Sam was ~20k inference requests/day with median input length ~120 tokens and peak QPS ~35 for batch jobs. You mentioned spikes during model retraining windows where sustained throughput could double for a few hours.

3) SLOs & latency: target 95p latency <= 300ms for interactive queries; can tolerate higher latency for asynchronous batch reranks.

4) Compliance: SOC2 and basic audit logs are required; potential future need for HIPAA assessment.

5) Commercial ask: want a sense of unit economics (hosted per-token vs reserved Dedicated capacity) and a simple cost model for the three paths (Hosted API -> Dedicated reserved commit -> Private VPC/on-prem).

Next steps from our side: I will send a couple of scenario-based cost comparisons (attached) that show break-even points between per-token hosted pricing and monthly reserved capacity at a few usage tiers. Also including an initial Dedicated config and a Private deployment checklist (networking, KMS, air-gapped notes).

Can you confirm the monthly token estimate you expect (tokens in + tokens out)? If you prefer, Sam, a sample week of traffic CSV would let us produce a more detailed cost projection — I attached a small template (velox_usage_report.csv) you can drop into.

Proposed next meeting: 30-minute pricing review week of Nov 2 — any time Tue/Wed afternoon PT works for us.

Thanks — looking forward.

Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya, this is helpful. A few clarifications: 

- Confirming the target token volume: for month 1 we expect ~45M tokens in+out (pilot with ~2M events), and steady-state year 1 estimate is ~400M tokens/month if we enable more features.
- Residency: we must keep all user PII in our AWS VPC for the pilot; we can evaluate a Hosted path only for anonymized / aggregated pipelines. So the hybrid approach sounds right (start hosted for non-PII, Dedicated/private for PII).
- Latency: 300ms 95p is ideal for the UI flows. For background ranking jobs we accept >1s.

I'm attaching our anonymized weekly sample. Sam will drop the CSV into the template you sent. Can you highlight assumptions you used in the cost model (e.g., tokens per request, average latencies, CPU/GPU assumptions) so we can compare apples-to-apples with our internal forecast?

Dana

Subject: Pricing scenarios attached (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Dana / Sam — attaching a short set of scenarios (pricing_scenarios.xlsx) and a PDF summary (redwood_dedicated_pricing.pdf). Key assumptions I used (please validate):

- Token math: 120 tokens in + 80 tokens out = 200 tokens per request (based on call).
- Monthly tokens: Pilot = 45M; Steady = 400M.
- Hosted per-token list: $0.0004 per token for generation (example blended rate for our hosted catalog).
- Dedicated reserved: we modeled a 4x A100 equivalent pool (4 x A100 40GB) with a monthly reserved commit at $X/month (see PDF). Effective per-token cost under Dedicated depends on utilization; at 70% sustained utilization the per-token compute costs drop ~3-4x vs hosted.
- Private VPC / On-prem: one-time infra + monthly ops; pricing is customized — we included a simple TCO line (hardware + 18% infra ops).

High-level outputs from the attached workbook: 
- Pilot (45M tokens/month): Hosted per-token is cheapest for pilot since reserved commit amortization is high. Hosted estimate ~ $18k/month (45M * 0.0004). Dedicated reserved commit starts to make sense above ~120–150M tokens/month depending on target latency and utilization.
- Steady (400M tokens/month): Dedicated reserved at 4-GPU pool shows 2.5–3x lower per-token compute cost vs hosted after commit; total bill depends on whether you need dedicated SLAs/SLOs and data-residency options.
- Private: becomes cost-competitive at larger scale (>= 800M tokens/month) if you can bear upfront hardware/ops and stricter residency needs.

I'll highlight a couple of concrete plan options in the workbook: 
A) Hybrid (Recommended initial): Keep non-PII pipelines on Hosted for agility; reserve a small Dedicated pool for PII traffic and work toward a Private VPC for full residency later.
B) Dedicated-first: If your compliance/legal team requires no cloud-hosted PII from day one, we can work on Dedicated + Private migration plan, but initial commit sizes increase unit economics break-even.

Attachment: pricing_scenarios.xlsx (stub), redwood_dedicated_pricing.pdf (stub)

Let me know if you'd like a short walkthrough of the workbook. I'm available Tue Nov 3 at 10:30am PT or Wed Nov 4 at 2:00pm PT.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Pricing scenarios attached (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks for the details — great framing Aditya. Internal notes and next steps below.

Internal summary (Marissa -> AE/Go-to-Market):
- Pilot at 45M/month: recommend Hosted for anonymized pipelines (fastest path) + small Dedicated reserved pool sized to handle PII peak traffic with autoscaling buffer. This avoids a large up-front commit and keeps day-1 latency SLOs achievable.
- For the Steady 400M/month case: build a forecasted Dedicated sizing plan (we should model both 4-GPU and 8-GPU options) including burst capacity and can propose a stepped commit (3-month ramp schedule).
- Private/on-prem: prepare a high-level TCO and an implementation checklist (networking, KMS, audit/log shipping). We should also flag potential HIPAA scoping if Velox confirms PHI.

Action items: 
1) Aditya: share the populated pricing_scenarios.xlsx with the Velox CSV merged (they said Sam will drop it into the template).
2) Neha: can you run a quick Dedicated sizing calc for 400M tokens/month and produce a 4 vs 8 GPU cost sheet? Use the kernel/latency assumptions Aditya used.
3) Marissa: I'll own the Private deployment checklist and TCO doc; I'll draft an executive summary for the Nov 3 meeting.

Dana / Sam — we'd like to propose Tue Nov 3 at 10:30am PT for a 30-minute pricing walkthrough. If that works please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite + dial-in. 

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
